One semantic check before this settles: keeping the optional pq_binding failure from invalidating the underlying signed proof is right.
But please keep the PQ-binding evidence itself three-way. A real binding mismatch / expected-but-unbound wallet and an RPC/gateway outage are different facts:
verified != refuted != unverifiable
So checks.pq_binding_verified = false should not be the only observable for both “checked and failed” and “could not check”. A separate pq_binding_evidence (plus a machine-readable reason for unverifiable) would preserve the same evidence/decision separation already pinned in ERC-8373.
The overall proof may remain valid because the check is optional; the stronger provenance claim simply remains unestablished when the PQ-binding check is unavailable.

You're right, and it was a real bug, not just a naming nit. verify_pq_binding() had a branch (malformed/missing gateway statement, on-chain shows a real binding exists) that returned verified=False -- which routes/execution.py then used to flip valid=False on the whole signed proof, even though nothing was actually refuted, the check just couldn't complete.

Fixed: added a single evidence field (verified/refuted/unverifiable) that verified is now strictly derived from, so they can't drift apart again, plus a machine-readable reason code (no_onchain_binding, hash_mismatch_onchain, hash_mismatch_gateway for refuted; network_unreachable, gateway_unreachable, onchain_unreachable, malformed_gateway_statement, invalid_address_format for unverifiable). checks.pq_binding_evidence is now its own top-level field in /verify-proof, not buried in the disclosure text.
